items.title: After 7 months, Glasswing overwhelms maintainers with underwhelming findings
items.summary: VulnCheck tracked 442 CVEs attributable to Anthropic's Project Glasswing, noting that only two have been exploited in the wild and that the project's ledger shows 1,654 duplicates and 419 withdrawn findings against just 217 fixes. The analysis highlights that Anthropic's OSS Scanner shifts validation work to maintainers, with curl rejecting 19 of 34 published reports as vulnerabilities.
items.why_it_matters: The data reveals a widening gap between discovery and remediation, with duplicates outnumbering fixes by nearly eight to one, and questions the accuracy of the claimed 94.2% true positive rate given the volume of withdrawn and duplicate entries.
items.next_step_detail: Read the post and review the linked CVE entries for any packages you use.
items.verification_note: the claimed 94.2% true positive rate is inaccurate given the volume of withdrawn and duplicate entries

items.title: Dev log # 29 The Review Marathon: Hardening libp2p across C# and Python
items.summary: Security hardening for the dotnet-libp2p and py-libp2p libraries included bounding memory usage, validating protocol inputs, and fixing resource leaks in swarm and yamux implementations. Specific fixes addressed unbounded key storage, TCP receive buffer retention, and the distinction between stream resets and clean EOFs.
items.why_it_matters: These changes prevent remote nodes from crashing local instances via memory exhaustion and ensure correct error handling during cross-language peer communication.
items.next_step_detail: Upgrade libp2p to the latest released version (e.g., pip install --upgrade libp2p).

items.title: From Attention to 3-Bit Caches: How LLMs Learned to Remember Less (MHA, GQA, MLA, MoE, Quantisation Explained)
items.summary: The text details how techniques like KV caching, grouped query attention, and quantization address the memory bottlenecks of transformer models, which require 16 GB per conversation for long contexts. It explains that these methods shrink, share, or sidestep the storage of keys and values to make inference feasible.
items.why_it_matters: The text offers a technical explanation of how these specific architectural changes reduce the memory footprint required for long-context inference.
items.next_step_detail: Read the article to identify quantisation strategies applicable to your model stack.

items.title: Stop Trusting npm Scans: Run Untrusted Packages in an Isolated AWS Sandbox
items.summary: RepoPilot is a Strands agent that uses a new run_in_sandbox tool to execute npm installs in a disposable AWS CodeBuild container, capturing real build logs to detect malicious post-install scripts that static analysis misses. The tool returns a JSON result containing the install status and specific supply-chain dangers found in the executed log.
items.why_it_matters: It prevents supply-chain attacks by ensuring untrusted code executes in an isolated AWS environment rather than on the developer's machine, providing evidence-based safety verdicts instead of static guesses.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and execute the provided CodeBuild sandbox script against a suspect package.

items.title: HF Paper: Infrathon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Real-World, Long-Horizon AI Infra Optimization
items.summary: Infrathon is a benchmark of diverse, long-horizon AI infrastructure optimization tasks that evaluates six models across 150 runs with 24-hour budgets. The framework provides resources for constructing these tasks, evaluating frontier agents, and discovering infrastructure solutions.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a method to evaluate whether frontier agents can continually improve real-world AI infrastructure over long horizons, revealing that shorter evaluations can overlook optimization gains and changes in relative model performance.

items.title: Cheapest AI API: 6 Options Compared for Real Workloads
items.summary: The article compares six AI inference APIs—Bearer Club, Mistral, Together AI, Groq, DeepSeek, and OpenRouter—based on pricing models, model access, data policies, and OpenAI SDK compatibility. It highlights that actual costs depend on token rates, access restrictions, and subscription fees rather than headline prices alone.
items.why_it_matters: Selecting the right API requires measuring cost per successful output against specific workload requirements, as low per-token rates can be negated by high failure rates, data-sharing mandates, or membership fees.
items.next_step_detail: Read the article and note the pricing table to decide which API to benchmark in your next deployment.

items.title: ArXiv: Can KV Cache Be Reused Across Model Updates? A DeepSeek-V4-Flash Case Study
items.summary: This paper investigates whether key-value attention caches can be reused across language model updates, using DeepSeek-V4-Flash as a case study. It finds that while caches retain useful task information, they do not faithfully reproduce the updated model's behavior, with retrieval accuracy varying from near-native performance to large losses.
items.why_it_matters: Direct cache reuse achieves median time-to-first-token speedups of 2.10–5.08× on three longer-prefix QA benchmarks, offering a quantifiable latency reduction for inference workloads.
items.next_step_detail: Read the abstract and experiment section to assess applicability to your inference pipeline.

items.title: JuliusBrussee/caveman
items.summary: Caveman is a Node.js CLI tool that compresses AI agent output and input logs using a controlled English style to reduce token counts, such as shrinking a 63-token explanation to 20 tokens. It operates locally across multiple agents like Claude Code and Codex, with measured results showing up to 54% cost reduction and 33.2% fewer input tokens per session.
items.why_it_matters: It lowers inference costs and reduces latency by minimizing the volume of tokens processed during coding agent sessions without altering the underlying code or technical accuracy.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run the example script to compare token counts against a standard prompt.

items.title: ArXiv: Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution
items.summary: PASE is a program-aided framework that evolves LLM agent skills by separating reusable procedural logic into editable programs, allowing targeted updates without modifying model parameters. Experiments show PASE consistently outperforms baselines by over 2.8% and exhibits greater evolutionary stability and generalization capability.
items.why_it_matters: It addresses the difficulty of maintaining skills represented as natural language documents by enabling targeted updates to executable components, which reduces the need to repeatedly revise descriptive knowledge.
items.next_step_detail: Read the abstract and method section to assess integration into your skill library.

items.title: ArXiv: HandsOnAid: Building and Evaluating an Offline First-Aid Assistant for Emergency Response Scenarios
items.summary: HandsOnAid is a 4-bit Gemma 2B model fine-tuned with QLoRA on the FirstAidQA dataset to provide offline first-aid advice on smartphones without network connectivity. The system was evaluated using a strict rubric and LLM judges, with the best configuration achieving a score of 2.51 out of 5.
items.why_it_matters: The study provides measured latency data (6.86 seconds to first token, 14.88 seconds for a complete answer) for running a fine-tuned 4-bit LLM on a Pixel 7 Pro with six CPU threads and no network connection.
items.next_step_detail: Download the paper to understand the fine‑tuning pipeline and dataset construction.
